summary: 1928 steel tower built by the Speir Pine Lumber Company, later transferred to the Georgia Forestry Commission; NHLR says it remains in active service at a state ranger station in Clinch County.

facts.design: 100-foot International Stacey steel tower with 7 by 7 foot metal cab

staffing.status: remains in active service (NHLR description, which carries no date); current staffing not in the sources

access.note: Sits at a state ranger station; the sources call it a local attraction but give no visiting rules

visit.trail_note: Located at a state ranger station; the sources do not say whether the tower may be climbed

events.note: Built by the Speir Pine Lumber Company to protect pinelands west of the Okefenokee; Forest Lookouts says a private lumbering company erected it
Registered September 1, 1999; nominator listed as unknown
Bugaboo fire threatened the town of Fargo in April and May 2007; the sources do not say how the tower was involved

notes_for_editor: Current status and staffing rest on the NHLR line that the tower remains in active service; the NHLR description carries no date, and no GFC or news source on current use was found. The Vanishing Georgia free text stops at a subscription paywall. It calls the tower very relevant in the same passage as the Bugaboo fire threat but does not explain the link, so the story does not claim one. Wikipedia says Bugaboo Fire; Vanishing Georgia says Bugaboo Scrub Fire. Access marked restricted is an inference from the ranger-station location, not a stated rule.
